title: stage manifest
description: What a stage provider offers: the provider (id, version, the argv prefix that list --json and apply are appended to) and its stages. sapphire prints it natively for `stage list --json`; tools/handoff.py builds it from `vfx list --json` with the vfx-list adapter; a plugin may also ship it as a file named *.stage.json. A consumer refuses a manifest whose contract major it does not know and a stage whose geometry value it does not know. Identical in every repository that follows the convention.

contract.description: frames/1 or frames/2; a consumer refuses another major.

id.description: Lower case id; a registered tool uses its contracts/tool.json id.

version.description: The provider's version text, for example the first line of --version.

command.description: The argv prefix: the program, then fixed words. `list --json` and `apply STAGE ...` are appended to it. In a *.stage.json file a relative program path is relative to the file's folder.

id.description: The stage id passed to apply; a leading @ marks a built in stage of a wrapper (for example @ffmpeg-filter).

kind.description: frame: output frame N depends on input frame N only; temporal: output frames depend on several input frames.

spool.description: true when the stage reads its whole input before it writes the first frame (it is silent while it spools, so a wrapper must not judge it by a stall timeout).

geometry.description: preserve: width, height, fps and pixel format of the output equal the input. declared: the stage answers apply STAGE --describe with its output geometry. Any other value is a valid manifest, but a consumer refuses that stage.

depths.description: Bits per channel the stage accepts: 8 rgba, 16 rgba64le, 32 gbrapf32le.

params.description: Parameters as --param K=V. Keys beyond id, kind and default (name, choices, min, max, precision) pass through unchanged.
